items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And it was marvelous, introduced by a wonderful broadcasting person called Wilford Thomas, who was an Australian and he had a kind of a nice broadcasting voice you know, it wasn’t that usual English plummy, kind of teeth-in-the-back-of-your-throat voice.

ctx.x: It’s funny you mention Derek, because I remember listening — there was a program on the BBC, it was a wonderful program, we had some marvelous musicians, you know I’m not talking about these trad people, but people like Kenny Baker and Bruce Turner and George Chisolm and people like that. And Kenny Baker is a wonderful trumpet player. And there was a program on the BBC called “Kenny Baker’s Dozen.” And this was in the

days of live radio you know, none of this taping and stuff. And it was really live. And these guys were in the studio and Derek used to play piano with them sometimes. And it used to be either Norman Stenfalt, and I’d be listening for the piano player, lying in bed you know, I suppose I’d done my homework and I’m going to school the next morning. “Kenny Baker’s Dozen” would come on once a week, some night, round about eleven o’clock. And it was marvelous, introduced by a wonderful broadcasting person called…
So did you find friends of a like nature who were getting into this music?
